answer: Cross-Reference Forcing. Each identity publishes a small set of links to independent peers; the protocol requires every link to be reciprocated within a fixed window, and a refusal or timeout flags the pair. Because a sybil cluster must cross-link only to itself, its internal edge density exceeds what honest, orchard-like sparse graphs show, so the cluster stands out as a dense marble amid scattered nodes. Duplicating one identity therefore requires the attacker to maintain verifiable reciprocal links at every summit of the fake graph,
